summary30s: In July 1991, Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh initiated structural economic reforms (LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation).
The Ayodhya dispute culminated in the demolition of the Babri Masjid on 6 December 1992, leading to nationwide communal violence and the dismissal of BJP state governments under Article 356.
The February 2002 Godhra train burning triggered catastrophic anti-Muslim violence in Gujarat, prompting the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) to intervene.

Despite bitter electoral rhetoric, a broad four-point consensus emerged across all major parties: (1) Economic reforms, (2) OBC reservations, (3) Role of regional parties, (4) Pragmatic non-ideological coalitions.
Indian democracy deepened through the 'Second Democratic Upsurge', shifting political power towards backward classes, Dalits, and regional sub-nationalisms.

coreConcepts.title: The 1991 New Economic Policy (LPG)
coreConcepts.explanation: Facing a critical Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis in mid-1991 (foreign exchange reserves down to barely two weeks of imports), the Congress government headed by P.V. Narasimha Rao with Dr. Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister initiated sweeping structural adjustment reforms. Known as LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation), the New Economic Policy dismantled the 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj', drastically lowered customs duties, devalued the rupee, opened sectors to Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), and divested loss-making public enterprises. Despite initial opposition from trade unions, the Left, and Swadeshi groups, economic growth accelerated, and every successive government (United Front, NDA, UPA) continued the reform trajectory.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 1
coreConcepts.examTip: New Economic Policy launched in July 1991 by PM P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

coreConcepts.title: The Ayodhya Dispute and the Rise of Hindutva Politics
coreConcepts.explanation: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh's successor, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP, formed 1980 under Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani), adopted 'Hindutva' (cultural nationalism coined by V.D. Savarkar). In February 1986, the Faizabad District Court ordered the unlocking of the gates of the Babri Masjid structure, allowing Hindus to offer prayers. Mobilization intensified: L.K. Advani led a massive 'Somnath to Ayodhya Rath Yatra' in September-October 1990. On 6 December 1992, kar sevaks gathered in Ayodhya and demolished the 16th-century Babri Masjid. Riots erupted in Mumbai and across India. The Central Government dismissed four BJP state governments (UP, MP, Rajasthan, HP) under Article 356 and appointed the Liberhan Commission to investigate the demolition.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 2
coreConcepts.examTip: Demolition of Babri Masjid: 6 December 1992. Investigated by the Liberhan Commission (which submitted its report in 2009).

coreConcepts.title: The Gujarat Riots of 2002 and Human Rights Oversight
coreConcepts.explanation: In February-March 2002, large-scale communal violence broke out in Gujarat. The trigger occurred on 27 February 2002 at Godhra railway station, where a bogie of the Sabarmati Express carrying kar sevaks returning from Ayodhya was set on fire, killing 57 people. In the retaliatory anti-Muslim pogrom that followed, over 1,000 people (mostly Muslims) were killed, women assaulted, and homes destroyed. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) severely criticized the state government for its failure to control violence, protect citizens, and prosecute culprits. The Supreme Court intervened to transfer high-profile cases (e.g., Best Bakery case) out of Gujarat to ensure fair trials, highlighting the role of constitutional bodies in defending secular democratic norms.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 3
coreConcepts.examTip: The Godhra train burning incident occurred on 27 February 2002, triggering the communal violence in Gujarat.

coreConcepts.title: The Four Areas of Growing Political Consensus
coreConcepts.explanation: Despite fierce competitive rhetoric, political scientists identify four crucial elements of consensus among major political parties in India since the 1990s: (1) Agreement on New Economic Policies: All major parties (including regional ones and initially reluctant Left/Swadeshi factions) support economic liberalisation and believe it leads to prosperity; (2) Acceptance of Political and Social Claims of Backward Castes (OBCs): All parties accept reservation of seats for OBCs in education and employment as essential social justice; (3) Acceptance of the Role of State-level (Regional) Parties: Regional parties are acknowledged as legitimate partners in running the national government; (4) Pragmatic Governance over Ideology: Coalitions are formed based on power-sharing agreements rather than rigid ideological alignment (e.g., secular parties allying with BJP, or sworn rivals sharing coalitions).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 4: 'Growing Consensus'
coreConcepts.examTip: CUET direct question: 'Which of the following is NOT one of the four areas of consensus in Indian politics since the 1990s?'

diagram.caption: The four-point consensus governing Indian governance from the 1990s to the 2020s

  <text x="65" y="166" fill="#14532d" fontSize="11">• High GDP growth prioritized over state control</text>

workedExamples.question:
Which Commission of Inquiry was appointed by the Government of India to investigate the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya on 6 December 1992?
(A) Sarkaria Commission
(B) Liberhan Commission
(C) Shah Commission
(D) Nanavati Commission
workedExamples.explanation: Following the demolition of the Babri Masjid on 6 December 1992, the Central Government appointed the Liberhan Commission headed by retired High Court Judge M.S. Liberhan to investigate the sequence of events.
solutionStepByStep: Step 3: Nanavati Commission = 1984 anti-Sikh riots & 2002 Godhra.
Step 4: Liberhan Commission = Babri Masjid demolition.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Commission of Inquiry identification in communal flashpoints.
solutionSteps: Step 3: Nanavati Commission = 1984 anti-Sikh riots & 2002 Godhra.
Step 4: Liberhan Commission = Babri Masjid demolition.

workedExamples.question:
Which of the following was NOT one of the four areas of growing consensus among political parties in India since the 1990s?
(A) Acceptance of the New Economic Policies (reforms)
(B) Acceptance of the political and social claims of the Other Backward Classes (OBCs)
(C) Acceptance of complete privatization of defence and nuclear weapons
(D) Acceptance of the crucial role of state-level regional parties in governance
workedExamples.explanation: According to NCERT Chapter 9, the four areas of consensus are: (1) New economic policies, (2) Acceptance of OBC claims, (3) Acceptance of the role of state-level parties, and (4) Emphasis on pragmatic alliances rather than ideological purity. Privatization of nuclear weapons is absurd and not part of any consensus.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Recall the 4-point consensus list from NCERT Chapter 9.
Step 3: Option C is completely false.
Conclusion: Option C is the correct answer.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Except-pattern question on four-point political consensus.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Recall the 4-point consensus list from NCERT Chapter 9.
Step 3: Option C is completely false.
Conclusion: Option C is the correct answer.

commonTraps.misconception: Thinking the BJP was the only party that opposed the New Economic Policy in 1991.
commonTraps.correctConcept: The Left Front, trade unions, and even sections within Congress opposed the reforms in 1991. The BJP had some Swadeshi critics, but broadly supported deregulation and private enterprise.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask which ideological group consistently questioned economic globalization.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: The Left Front was the most consistent and ideological critic of 1991 liberalisation.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing coalition governments slowed down India's economic growth.
commonTraps.correctConcept: Between 1989 and 2014, under various coalition regimes (UF, NDA, UPA), India's economy experienced its highest sustained growth rates, averaging 7-8% annually.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Students confuse political instability with economic deceleration.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Economic reforms and high GDP growth continued uninterrupted under coalitions.

practiceQuestions.question: In July 1991, who was the Finance Minister of India who presented the historic budget initiating the New Economic Policy (LPG)?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister in the P.V. Narasimha Rao government who introduced the structural reforms in July 1991.

practiceQuestions.question: On which date was the 16th-century Babri Masjid in Ayodhya demolished by kar sevaks?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Babri Masjid was demolished on 6 December 1992 by thousands of kar sevaks.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the BJP leader who led the famous 'Rath Yatra' from Somnath in Gujarat to Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh in September-October 1990?
practiceQuestions.explanation: L.K. Advani led the historic Rath Yatra from Somnath to Ayodhya in the autumn of 1990.

practiceQuestions.question: Which Constitutional Commission intervened forcefully during the 2002 Gujarat riots, rebuking the state government for failing to protect innocent citizens?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) criticized the Gujarat government's handling of the communal violence.

practiceQuestions.question: In 1986, which court passed the order directing that the locks of the Babri Masjid premises be opened so that Hindus could offer worship?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In February 1986, the Faizabad District Court ordered that the gates of the Babri Masjid structure be opened for Hindu worshippers.

practiceQuestions.question: What does the abbreviation 'LPG' stand for in the context of the 1991 New Economic Policy?
practiceQuestions.explanation: LPG in economic policy refers to Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation.

practiceQuestions.question: Following the demolition of the Babri Masjid in December 1992, the Union Government dismissed how many BJP-ruled state governments under Article 356?

options.text: 4 (Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Himachal Pradesh)

practiceQuestions.explanation: The Central government dismissed the BJP governments in UP, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Himachal Pradesh under Article 356.

practiceQuestions.question: Which famous case was transferred out of Gujarat to Maharashtra by the Supreme Court of India in 2004 to ensure a fair trial for victims of the 2002 riots?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Supreme Court transferred the Best Bakery trial from Gujarat to Maharashtra in a landmark intervention for justice.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the Prime Minister of India who led the minority Congress government that implemented the historic 1991 economic reforms?
practiceQuestions.explanation: P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister from 1991 to 1996 who piloted the reforms.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Successive coalition governments of differing ideological complexions (United Front, NDA, UPA) sustained and expanded the 1991 economic reforms.
Reason (R): A broad political consensus emerged that economic liberalisation, global integration, and private capital investments were essential to generate wealth, employment, and infrastructure.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Despite political rivalries, all major coalitions agreed on the imperative of economic reforms. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
